output.brief: The rejections trace to a data error, not the fungicide, Lower Serra fruit, or the carrier. When Meridane bookings moved to the new documentation system on 4 Aug, the mandarin product record had been copied from avocados. It carried a 7.0°C carriage temperature instead of your 4.0°C specification. The system sent that to Meridane automatically. Meridane's units held 7°C as instructed. All five Meridane containers sent that way (K3, K4, K6, K8, K9) were rejected. Every container at 4°C passed, including Pellacor-treated Coastway loads (K5, K7). Meridane's own units therefore did not fail, and Pellacor did not fail either. K3 used old fungicide and was still rejected. Lower Serra pallets were worse inside the rejected containers, but there is no comparison in accepted containers, so treat that as unproven. Do next: correct the temperature in the product record today. Have Meridane reset the container now at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check comparing booking temperature with the product specification. Do not suspend growers, file the cargo claim, revert the fungicide, or penalise the contractor yet. The cooperative's own sign-off reviewed the product record. Confidence is high.
